title: Define past and future windows before modeling to prevent leakage
when_to_use: When building a predictive model that requires forecasting future customer behavior or value.
experience:
- **Explicitly set a cutoff date** to separate historical data (feature window) from future data (label/target window).
- **Construct features using only data from a defined past window** (e.g., last 6 months) relative to the cutoff.
- **Construct labels using only data from a defined future window** (e.g., next 3 months) after the cutoff.
- **Ensure each prediction entity (account/visitor) has enough data in both windows** to be included in training.
- **Implement a time-based data split** (e.g., train/validation/test) respecting the temporal order to avoid look-ahead bias.
- **Create a verification script** that confirms no future information is used in feature calculation.
checklist: Establish a clear cutoff date and logic
Compute features using only past-window data
Compute labels using only future-window data
common_failure_prevented: Using aggregated lifetime features for prediction, which leaks future information and inflates model performance.

title: Construct labels from future performance for predictive tasks
when_to_use: When the goal is to predict a future state (e.g., high-value, churn) and a ground truth label is not directly provided.
experience:
- **Identify the target KPI** to be predicted (e.g., future engagement minutes, revenue, retention status).
- **Define a future observation window** (e.g., next 3 months) for calculating the target KPI.
- **Derive the binary or continuous label** from the future KPI (e.g., high-value = top 25% of future minutes).
- **Calculate label thresholds dynamically per time window** if using rolling windows, not a single global threshold.
- **Explicitly document the label definition logic** (including thresholds and time windows) to ensure reproducibility.
- **Validate label distribution** to ensure it's not imbalanced or trivial.
checklist: Set future window for label calculation
Create label using percentiles or thresholds
common_failure_prevented: Defining high-value customers using historical aggregates instead of future performance, making the prediction task circular.

title: Build and evaluate a supervised model, not just a heuristic score
when_to_use: When tasked with improving prediction accuracy or building a classification/regression model.
experience:
- **Choose an appropriate supervised algorithm** (e.g., Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost) for the task (classification/regression).
- **Split data into train/validation/test sets** using chronological or random splits while preventing leakage.
- **Train the model** on the training set using the defined features and labels.
- **Evaluate on a held-out set** using relevant metrics (e.g., Precision, Recall, AUC-ROC, RMSE).
- **Compare model performance against a baseline** (e.g., existing model, simple heuristic) to demonstrate improvement.
- **Report feature importance** to provide interpretability and business insights.
common_failure_prevented: Proposing a simple weighted composite score without proper training and validation, failing to meet accuracy targets.
